key_insight: An AI-guided discovery pipeline identified four novel bimetallic alloys with DFT-validated, near-thermoneutral hydrogen binding as promising hydrogen evolution reaction catalysts.
engineering_relevance: Generative design and consensus screening can prioritize alloy compositions beyond existing databases, focusing costly DFT calculations and experimental follow-up.
method: Fine-tune MatterGen on adsorption-labelled bulk alloys to generate novel binary structures targeting near-zero hydrogen adsorption energy.
Use MatterSim to assess stability, rank low-index facets, and relax hydrogen-covered slabs.
Combine MEGNet–ALIGNN agreement with MatterSim energy-difference checks to shortlist candidates for DFT validation.
evidence_signal: Of eight DFT-tested alloys, Pd5Au, Pt5Rh, Cu5Pt3, and Pd13Ru3 showed hydrogen binding within the thermoneutral window; all eight were dynamically stable in phonon calculations.
watch_item: Near-thermoneutral binding and phonon stability do not establish experimental HER activity, operating durability, or affordability; the four highlighted alloys all contain precious metals.
paper_title: Generative Design and Graph Neural Network Screening of Novel Bimetallic Alloy Catalysts for the Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
